doc.title: Crescent City Crystals: Dave Bailey, Harold Christophe, Albert Delone, Sylvester Handy Interview, 1963-11-13

chapter: Dave Bailey: brass bands and playing career
title: Chris Kelly, the Gibson band and brass bands under Jimmy Jackson
summary: Bailey names Chris Kelly and Stutter as his main bands and discusses brass band work, Jimmy Jackson who managed the band, and picking up bass drum himself.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: What, um, can you remember any other bands you worked with? For long periods?
I played with Chris Kelley and Stutter.
The only ones, two bands I played with, Ray Zan, Stutter, my brother and Chris Kelley. Gibson band?
Hmm? Don't you work with the Gibson band, Stutter?
No, I don't have been playing with them, I only forgot to hold on. See, I just played with them, they just got the brass band, I played with the brass band.
Yeah, that's what I mean. I worked with them, Stutter. Yeah, you've been with them. I mean, Austin.
I worked with Stutter. What brass bands, what brass bands you worked with?
I worked with, uh, that's the only two brass bands I worked with. No, three. Yeah. A fellow named Jimmy Jackson, he died. Uh-huh.
What instrument did he play? Well, he used to play snare drum.
No, he used to play any stuff, and he hired me, he had given up and just, get in the jaws, man, it's a band.
Who taught you to play bass drum, anybody? No. You just picked that up?
I picked it up myself. That's a gift from God.
